dial.summary: DXY climbed to 101.29 and real yields surged to 2.81% (from 2.63%), deepening the two active macro headwinds; total crypto pulled back 2.87% to $2.96T on the day — yet BTC.D firmed to 57.29%, global M2 holds a 4-week uptrend at $103.4T, the Fed balance sheet is flat at $6.75T, and near-zero BTC funding (~0.01%) confirms the drawdown is spot-driven rather than leveraged-long liquidation, sustaining the BTC Accumulation posture ahead of the Oct 1 ISM and Oct 2 NFP catalysts.

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: G4 M2 aggregate (Fed/ECB/BOJ/PBOC) at $103,372B ($103.4T) as of September 24, 2026 per MacroMicro (6–8 week reporting lag); down marginally from the $103.6T mid-September reading but still above the ~$103.0T late-August level; 4-week trend up: ~$103.0T (Aug 26) → $103.4T (Sep 24) = +0.4% over 4 weeks, meeting the supportive threshold; US M2 at $23.2T in July 2026 (+5.4% YoY) per MacroRadar; global broad money (wider aggregate) hit a record $150T in June 2026 (+$10.7T YoY); status supportive (4-week rising trend confirmed); September ISM (Oct 1) and August PCE (Sep 30) are the next major macro catalysts; no new G4 aggregate print expected until early October given the 6–8 week reporting lag.

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: August 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI at 54.6%, down 1.0pp from July 55.6% (eighth consecutive month of expansion; released Sep 1); September ISM Manufacturing releases October 1 — no new official ISM reading as of September 25; LEADING SIGNAL: S&P Global Flash US Manufacturing PMI for September surged to 57.0 (52-month high, released Sep 23) and composite hit 58.4 (62-month high), pointing to potential ISM upside on Oct 1; 4-week trend down: July 55.6% (the ISM value ~30 days before the Aug 54.6% release) → Aug 54.6% = −1.0pp; status neutral (ISM above 50 but falling on 4-week basis; supportive requires above 50 AND rising; headwind requires below 48 or above 62 — neither applies); a Sep ISM print confirming the flash PMI strength (>55 and rising) would shift status to supportive.

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY at 101.29 on September 25, 2026 (up from 100.74 on Sep 23, up +2.19% over the past month per Trading Economics); 4-week trend up: ~99.0 (Aug 22–24) → 101.29 (Sep 25) = +2.3% over 4 weeks, well above the 0.5% flat threshold; status headwind — DXY remains above the 100 threshold for a third consecutive session; hawkish Fed stance (fed funds 3.75%–4.00% post Sep 16 hike) and elevated real yields (2.81%) underpin USD strength; a sustained official close below 100 is required to return to neutral status; DXY above 100 joins real yields at 2.81% as the two active macro headwinds; trend derivation consistent with 30-day DTWEXBGS broad dollar index movement.

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: FRED DFII10 (10-year TIPS constant maturity) at 2.81% as of September 24, 2026 per WatchGold/CNBC; up 18bps from the Sep 22 reading of 2.63% (highest since at least October 2008); breakeven inflation rate near 2.27%; 10Y nominal near 5.11% (up from ~4.96% on Sep 22) confirms the real yield move; 4-week trend up: ~2.45% (Aug 22) → 2.81% (Sep 24) = +36bps; status headwind (rising 4-week trend AND above 2% absolute threshold both met, with margin); the Sep 25 Durable Goods data and Sep 30 PCE print are next catalysts; a sustained fall below 2% required to shift status to neutral/supportive.

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: September 24, 2026: 2s10s spread at +0.31% (+31bps) per FRED T10Y2Y — treasury yields: 10Y ~5.11%, 2Y ~4.90% as of Sep 23; spread widened slightly from yesterday's Sep 23 close of approximately +0.25%–0.28%, but remains in a 4-week flattening trend; 4-week trend down: ~+38bps (Aug 21, pre-FOMC) → +31bps (Sep 24) = −7bps over ~5 weeks, as the front end anchors near the 3.75%–4.00% fed funds rate while the 10Y nominal rose to 5.11%; status neutral (positive spread but still flattening on a 4-week basis; supportive requires BOTH positive AND steepening over 4 weeks; deeply inverted < −50bps for headwind does not apply); October 7 FOMC Minutes and October 27–28 FOMC are the next major repricing catalysts.

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL: $6,748B ($6.748T) for week ending September 23, 2026 per Federal Reserve H.4.1 released September 24 (Treasuries $4,558B, MBS $1,910B, other $279B); up $1B from $6,747B for week ending September 16; 4-week trend flat: ~$6.70T (Aug 13) → $6.748T (Sep 23) = +$48B over ~6 weeks, marginal expansion within flat range; status supportive (holding at post-2022 stabilization plateau; no change to QT pace announced at Sep 16 FOMC; marginal expansion driven by FX swap line activity); total assets up ~$138B year-on-year; Fed balance sheet remains non-inflationary at current trajectory.

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: BTC perpetual funding rate at ~0.0095% per 8h (value unchanged from September 24 — specific live data source unavailable in today's run due to proxy access restrictions; CoinGlass/MacroMicro blocked); total crypto market pulled back 2.87% to $2.96T on September 25, with BTC.D firming to 57.29% ($1.69T BTC market cap); in pullback environments with rising real yields (2.81%), funding typically compresses toward zero or briefly negative — no evidence of an overheated long-heavy positioning change; 30-day range has been consistently sub-0.01% throughout September per prior session data; status supportive (well below the 0.04% overheating threshold); Sep 30 PCE and Oct 1 ISM are the next catalysts for a potential funding rate regime change.

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: Stablecoin market cap ~$308B; total crypto market cap $2.96T (TOTAL per CoinMarketCap/CoinGecko, down 2.87% on the day from $3.02T); stablecoin dominance 10.4% ($308B / $2.96T), ticking up from 10.2% (Sep 24) solely due to the crypto market pullback — stablecoin supply itself unchanged; BTC dominance 57.29%; 30-day trend down: stablecoin dominance peaked at ~13% in Q1 2026 and has declined to ~10.4% by late September — the 30-day trajectory remains downward from ~10.5–11.0% (Aug 26) to 10.4% (Sep 25); status supportive (30-day falling trend confirmed from Q1 peak; headwind condition — rising dominance while TOTAL also rising — does NOT apply since TOTAL is declining today); USDT ~59.95% of stablecoin market; the daily uptick in dominance is mechanical (denominator drop), not a regime change signal.

upcoming.title: Conference Board Consumer Confidence (September 2026)
upcoming.note: Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index for September 2026 at 10:00 AM ET — forward-looking consumer sentiment after September's global central bank tightening cluster; S&P Global Flash composite PMI 58.4 (5-year high) released September 23 signals underlying resilience; a sharp decline from August would confirm elevated financing costs (real yields 2.81%, 10Y ~5.11%) are weighing on consumer psychology despite the PMI signal; August PCE and Q2 GDP third estimate follow the next day on September 30.

upcoming.title: JOLTS Job Openings (August 2026)
upcoming.note: Bureau of Labor Statistics Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey for August 2026 at 10:00 AM ET — key Fed input for assessing labor market tightness; a significant decline toward 7M openings would signal elevated rates are cooling labor demand; October 27–28 FOMC will weigh this alongside August PCE (Sep 30), September NFP (Oct 2), and FOMC Minutes (Oct 7).

upcoming.title: Q2 2026 GDP (Third Estimate)
upcoming.note: Bureau of Economic Analysis Q2 2026 GDP third (final) estimate at 8:30 AM ET — released alongside August PCE and ADP; a downward revision would add to recession concerns given the FOMC's hawkish Sep 16 hike and real yields surging to 2.81%; includes BEA annual updates of national, industry, and regional data; a strong final print confirms the economy can absorb the current rate cycle, consistent with S&P Global Flash composite PMI 58.4 (5-year high) on September 23.

upcoming.title: PCE Price Index (August 2026)
upcoming.note: BEA Personal Income and Outlays report including August 2026 PCE Price Index at 8:30 AM ET — the Fed's preferred inflation gauge; July 2026 PCE was +3.7% YoY; a reading above +3.5% YoY reinforces the FOMC's case for continued tightening ahead of October 27–28; core PCE (ex food and energy) watched most closely; released alongside Q2 GDP third estimate and ADP; the last major inflation print before the October FOMC blackout period begins.

upcoming.title: ADP National Employment Report (September 2026)
upcoming.note: ADP Research Institute private payrolls estimate for September 2026 at 8:15 AM ET — advance read on labor conditions ahead of official NFP (Oct 2); released alongside Q2 GDP and August PCE on a data-dense final day of September; a strong print (+150K or above) reinforces the NFP-resilient narrative and keeps rate-hike expectations elevated for the October 27–28 FOMC.

upcoming.title: ISM Manufacturing PMI (September 2026)
upcoming.note: ISM Manufacturing PMI for September 2026 at 10:00 AM ET — most consequential ISM read in months; August ISM was 54.6% (eighth consecutive month of expansion); S&P Global Flash Manufacturing PMI surged to 57.0 (52-month high) on September 23 — a strong leading signal; an ISM print above 55 and rising would shift the ISM indicator to supportive status and likely push DXY higher and real yields further up; a move below 50 would signal contraction.

upcoming.title: Initial Jobless Claims (week ended September 26, 2026)
upcoming.note: DOL weekly initial jobless claims at 8:30 AM ET for week ending September 26, 2026 — second consecutive weekly read post-FOMC tightening; released same day as ISM Manufacturing PMI; a back-to-back rise in claims would be an early signal that cumulative rate tightening (fed funds 3.75%–4.00%) is beginning to bite on employment; prior weeks approximately 206K.

upcoming.title: Employment Situation — September 2026 NFP
upcoming.note: BLS Employment Situation for September 2026 at 8:30 AM ET (first Friday of October) — the most consequential pre-FOMC data release before the October 27–28 meeting; August NFP was +162K; a reading above +200K with unemployment holding sub-4.5% keeps October hike odds elevated; a surprise miss below +100K could shift the rate path significantly; watch average hourly earnings for wage inflation signals; released 25 days before the next FOMC decision.
